cancer_indication: Breast cancer with RET fusions (metastatic disease; NCCN “useful in certain circumstances”).
moa: Selpercatinib binds directly to the ATP site of the RET kinase, preventing autophosphorylation and activation. In RET fusion–positive cells, this shuts off constitutive RET signaling that drives downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT pathways, reducing tumor cell proliferation and survival. In ER+ breast cancer, RET activation is linked to endocrine resistance; by inhibiting RET, selpercatinib can restore sensitivity to endocrine therapy and has shown re-sensitization effects in endocrine/CDK4/6 inhibitor–resistant models.

KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_RET_FUSION_KINASE_T.description: Constitutively active RET fusions drive downstream RAS/MAPK (MAPK/ERK) signaling.
KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_RET_FUSION_KINASE_T.interpretation:
RET fusion–driven MAPK/ERK signaling is a core proliferative pathway in RET-altered breast cancers and is a major downstream axis of oncogenic RET activity.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- RET signaling in ER⁺ BC activates MAPK and promotes endocrine resistance; RET fusions/overexpression act as oncogenic drivers, and selpercatinib provides deep and durable responses in RET-altered tumors (including a complete response in RET-fusion BC). A high KRAS/MAPK hallmark score mainly reflects RET pathway hyperactivation rather than intrinsic resistance, so these tumors are expected to be sensitive to selpercatinib.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (rare in breast cancer): a RET-fusion–driven tumor with high RET→RAS–ERK output is “oncogene-addicted,” so RET-selective inhibition is expected to be effective.
FDA label (RETEVMO; tumor-agnostic RET fusion): FDA 213246; NCT03157128; PMID:30446652; KEGG MEDICUS N00008; ChEMBL:CHEMBL4559134; DrugBank:DB15685 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: ERK pathway “Up” in breast cancer is often driven by non-RET oncogenes (e.g., ERBB2/EGFR/RAS/RAF), so RET inhibition may not suppress the dominant ERK driver.
PMID:30446652; ERK/MAPK signaling review; KEGG MEDICUS N00008 (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: a RET fusion may be present but underrepresented in bulk expression (low signature) or confined to a subclone; RET blockade can still produce benefit if the driver clone is clinically relevant.
FDA label (RET fusion solid tumors); PMID:30446652 (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: absence of RET-fusion ERK signaling implies no actionable RET dependence, so selpercatinib is unlikely to help in typical breast cancer.
Breast RET alterations context; pan-tumor RET fusion frequency (breast ~0.1%); PMID:30446652 (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: selpercatinib inhibits RET kinase activity, suppressing RET-fusion downstream MAPK (RAS–RAF–MEK–ERK) signaling and tumor proliferation/survival in RET-driven cancers.
FDA Approval Summary; FDA label; NCT03157128; KEGG MEDICUS N00008 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: pathway suppression can be observed, yet clinical resistance may persist due to parallel survival programs (e.g., PI3K dependency, anti-apoptotic rewiring) or inadequate exposure/PK in a heterogeneous tumor.
FDA label (exposure/toxicities); RET resistance reviews (FDA Access Data)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): a RET-selective inhibitor cannot increase functional RET→ERK signaling; any “Up” signature would reflect infiltrating/selected RET+ cells rather than increased signaling through inhibited RET.
FDA Approval Summary (MOA); selpercatinib binding/inhibition (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: acquired resistance can restore/maintain ERK output via on-target RET solvent-front mutations (e.g., G810) or RET-independent bypass (e.g., MET/KRAS amplification), yielding high ERK signaling with progression.
PMID:31988000; PMID:33007380; PMID:33082208; KEGG MEDICUS N00008 (PubMed)

KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_MUTATION_ACTIVATED_.description: Activated RET triggers downstream PI3K/AKT signaling that supports tumor cell survival and growth.
KEGG_MEDICUS_VARIANT_MUTATION_ACTIVATED_.interpretation:
PI3K/AKT signaling is a key survival pathway downstream of RET activation in RET-driven breast cancer contexts.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- RET activation can converge on mTOR/p70S6K and PI3K/AKT in ER⁺ BC, contributing to endocrine resistance. In non-breast RET-driven models, AKT–mTOR pathway upregulation is a mechanism of acquired resistance to selpercatinib that can be overcome with mTOR inhibition, suggesting that PI3K/AKT/mTOR hyperactivation not fully dependent on RET limits RET-TKI efficacy. In ER⁺ BC, co-targeting PI3K/AKT/mTOR (e.g. with everolimus or PI3Ki) plus endocrine therapy is already standard in some settings, so PI3K-high/RET-high tumors may need combinatorial approaches rather than selpercatinib alone.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (rare in breast cancer): if activated/altered RET drives PI3K–AKT survival signaling, pathway activation indicates RET dependence that is targetable by selpercatinib.
FDA label; FDA Approval Summary; KEGG “Mutation-activated RET to PI3K” network; ChEMBL/DrugBank IDs (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: PI3K signaling is frequently driven by PIK3CA/PTEN/RTKs in breast cancer; “Up” PI3K does not imply RET is the dominant driver, so RET inhibition may fail.
PI3K pathway background; breast RET context (KEGG)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: PI3K signature may be low in bulk despite RET dependence (e.g., subclonal RET activation, compensatory negative feedback); RET blockade can still be beneficial in true RET-driven disease.
FDA label (RET-driven solid tumors); breast RET alterations (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: low RET→PI3K signaling implies no RET-addiction; typical breast cancers will not respond to selpercatinib in this context.
Pan-tumor RET fusion rarity in breast; breast RET alterations (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: RET inhibition reduces downstream PI3K–AKT pro-survival signaling, contributing to tumor control in RET-altered cancers (tumor-agnostic RET fusion indication).
FDA Approval Summary; FDA label; NCT03157128 (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: even with reduced RET→PI3K output, tumors may persist via alternative PI3K inputs (e.g., ERBB2/IGF1R) or downstream lesions (PIK3CA/PTEN) that uncouple survival from RET.
PI3K pathway background; RET resistance (bypass) (KEGG)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): selpercatinib cannot increase RET-driven PI3K signaling; “Up” would represent compensatory/bypass activation rather than RET signaling enhancement by the drug.
FDA Approval Summary (RET inhibition MOA) (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: resistance frequently emerges through RET-independent bypass (e.g., MET amplification) that reactivates PI3K–AKT survival despite RET inhibition, yielding progressive disease with high PI3K signaling.
PMID:33007380; PMID:33082208; MET-dependent resistance evidence (PubMed)

HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.description: Cell-cycle transcriptional program driven by E2F-associated genes linked to proliferation.
HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS.interpretation:
E2F-driven cell-cycle activity reflects proliferative state in breast cancer models and is reported as suppressed in endocrine-resistant ER+ models upon RET inhibition.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- In ER⁺ BC models resistant to combined CDK4/6i + endocrine therapy, RET is upregulated; gene-set analysis shows enrichment of E2F targets and other proliferation programs. RET knockdown or pharmacologic inhibition (including selpercatinib in combination with CDK4/6i) reduces cell growth partly by downregulating E2F-controlled cell-cycle genes, making high E2F activity more of a RET-driven vulnerability than a resistance marker.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (rare, RET-driven subset): high proliferation/E2F program can reflect mitogenic RET signaling in RET-altered tumors; blocking RET can reduce E2F-driven cycling and produce response.
MSigDB HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (M5925); RET alterations in breast; selpercatinib MOA (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: strong E2F signaling may be driven by RB-pathway disruption/CDK activation or other oncogenes, making proliferation relatively RET-independent and limiting benefit from RET inhibition.
MSigDB HALLMARK_E2F_TARGETS (M5925); breast RET biology review context (GSEA MSigDB)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: low E2F signature (low cycling) can still coexist with an actionable RET fusion/driver in a subclone; selpercatinib may still shrink the RET-driven compartment.
FDA label (RET fusion solid tumors); breast RET alterations (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: low E2F activity plus no RET-driver implies limited dependence on RET-mediated mitogenic signaling and poor likelihood of response.
RET fusion rarity in breast; breast RET alterations (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: effective RET blockade suppresses mitogenic signaling, decreasing E2F target expression (cell-cycle entry) as part of a sensitive on-target response.
FDA Approval Summary (RET inhibition → downstream signaling blockade); MSigDB E2F set (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: a cytostatic decrease in proliferation can occur without durable tumor regression if survival is maintained via bypass pathways or downstream lesions, producing stable disease or early regrowth.
RET resistance mechanisms (RET-independent bypass common) (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): selpercatinib does not directly induce an E2F proliferation program; any “Up” would reflect clonal selection rather than a sensitivity mechanism.
FDA Approval Summary; MSigDB E2F set (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: resistant clones can sustain/increase E2F cycling via RET on-target mutations (e.g., G810) or bypass (MET/KRAS amplification), uncoupling proliferation from RET inhibition.
PMID:31988000; PMID:33007380; MSigDB E2F set (PubMed)

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene program associated with G2/M checkpoint control and mitotic progression.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation:
G2/M checkpoint regulators contribute to mitotic progression in breast cancer models and are reported as suppressed in resistant ER+ cell lines upon selpercatinib treatment.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- High G2/M pathway activity is associated with aggressive, metastatic-prone breast cancers. In CDK4/6i+ET-resistant ER⁺ models, RET overexpression sustains growth; RET knockdown enriches for downregulation of Hallmark G2M checkpoint and blocks G2–M progression. RET inhibition with selpercatinib plus CDK4/6i/fulvestrant resensitizes these models, indicating that tumors with G2/M-high, RET-driven proliferation can be sensitive to RET targeting.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (rare, RET-driven subset): high G2/M checkpoint signature reflects rapid cycling that can be driven by RET→MAPK/PI3K mitogenic input; RET inhibition can reduce cycling in RET-addicted tumors.
MSigDB HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT (M5901); selpercatinib MOA; breast RET alterations (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: high G2/M activity often reflects general aggressive biology (and non-RET drivers); if cycling is RET-independent, selpercatinib will not meaningfully impact the tumor.
MSigDB G2M set; breast RET biology review context (GSEA MSigDB)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: a less-proliferative tumor can still harbor an actionable RET fusion/driver; inhibition may benefit the RET-driven compartment even if G2/M signature is low.
FDA label; breast RET alterations (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: low G2/M plus absent RET driver suggests no RET-addiction and poor response likelihood in breast cancer.
RET fusion rarity in breast; breast RET alterations (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: on-target RET inhibition reduces proliferative signaling, lowering G2/M checkpoint gene expression as part of a sensitive pharmacodynamic response.
FDA Approval Summary; MSigDB G2M set (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: decreased cycling can occur yet resistance emerges through persistence/dormancy and later outgrowth driven by RET-independent survival or microenvironmental support.
RET resistance mechanisms overview (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): selpercatinib does not directly increase G2/M progression; “Up” would not be a mechanistic sensitivity outcome.
FDA Approval Summary; MSigDB G2M set (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: resistant disease maintains/increases cycling via on-target RET mutations or bypass signaling, preserving high G2/M activity despite therapy.
PMID:31988000; PMID:33007380; MSigDB G2M set (PubMed)

PID_RET_PATHWAY.description: RET (rearranged during transfection) receptor tyrosine kinase signaling pathway.
PID_RET_PATHWAY.interpretation:
Aberrant RET activity (fusions or amplifications/overexpression) can drive oncogenic signaling and is linked to therapeutic resistance (including endocrine resistance) in breast cancer contexts described.

Baseline-focused rationale:
- RET is overexpressed in a subset of ER⁺ BC and cooperates with ER to drive tumor growth. GDNF–RET signaling induces ER target genes and contributes to endocrine resistance, yet tumors often remain ER-positive/ER-driven. Preclinical work (e.g., RET inhibition with TKIs + aromatase inhibitors) and more recent data with selpercatinib in ER⁺/RET-high, CDK4/6i+ET-resistant models support dual targeting ER and RET, so a high estrogen-response hallmark can define a context where adding selpercatinib to endocrine therapy is rational. Your original “Down” assignment is inconsistent with this.

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate (rare in breast cancer): active RET signaling (including RET alterations reported in breast cancer) indicates potential RET dependence and susceptibility to selective RET inhibition.
MSigDB PID_RET_PATHWAY (M82; source PMID:18832364); breast RET alterations (PMID:30446652); selpercatinib MOA (GSEA MSigDB)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: RET-pathway gene expression can be elevated via ligand/paracrine RET activation in ER+ contexts (endocrine resistance biology) without being the dominant oncogenic driver, limiting response to RET TKIs alone.
ER+ RET/endocrine resistance; breast RET biology (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically rare: low bulk RET pathway may still mask an actionable RET fusion/driver present in a subclone; selective RET inhibition can still yield benefit if that clone drives progression.
FDA label; breast RET alterations (FDA Access Data)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: low RET signaling and no RET alteration implies no target engagement benefit, so selpercatinib is unlikely to be effective in most breast cancers.
Pan-tumor RET fusion rarity in breast; breast RET alterations (ScienceDirect)

Sensitive: Mechanistically accurate: selpercatinib directly inhibits RET kinase, reducing RET-pathway signaling as the intended pharmacodynamic effect associated with response in RET-driven tumors.
FDA Approval Summary; FDA label; MSigDB PID_RET_PATHWAY (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically rare: RET pathway suppression can occur, but progression can be driven by RET-independent mechanisms (e.g., MET/KRAS amplification) that sustain growth without RET signaling.
PMID:33007380; MET-dependent resistance evidence (PubMed)

Sensitive: Mechanistically not possible (direct effect): a RET inhibitor cannot increase functional RET signaling; observed “Up” would reflect sampling/clonal composition rather than drug-induced RET activation.
FDA Approval Summary; MSigDB PID_RET_PATHWAY (PMC)
Resistance: Mechanistically accurate: resistance can present with preserved/increased RET-pathway output via on-target resistance mutations or adaptive rewiring, correlating with lack of durable control.
PMID:31988000; PMID:33007380; MSigDB PID_RET_PATHWAY (PubMed)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: RET fusion–positive breast cancers and RET-driven tumor contexts are described as sensitive to RET inhibition, with clinical responses reported and mechanistic suppression of downstream MAPK/ERK and PI3K/AKT signaling upon RET blockade.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: TP53 is frequently co-mutated in RET-altered breast cancer (~80%), inactivating the p53 pathway; the deep-research output associates downregulated p53 pathway activity with increased resistance.

Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HR⁺/HER2⁻ (Luminal A/B): RET is more commonly overexpressed in ER⁺ tumors that have acquired endocrine resistance. Selpercatinib shows activity in this context (ER⁺ endocrine-resistant models and organoids were resensitized), and NCCN guidelines recognize RET fusions as actionable in HR⁺ metastatic disease (RET fusion → selpercatinib).
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.HER2⁺: RET genomic alterations have been identified in a subset of HER2⁺ tumors, though clinical data are limited. One index case with HER2+ breast cancer had a NCOA4-RET fusion and responded to RET inhibition (cabozantinib); the role of selpercatinib specifically in HER2+ cases is not documented.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.Triple-negative (Basal-like/HER2-enriche: A majority (~65%) of RET-altered breast cancers were ER⁻, implying many fall into the triple-negative category. Data in TNBC are sparse; selpercatinib’s tumor-agnostic approval suggests any RET fusion TNBC could respond, but no TNBC-specific trial results have been published.
Breast_cancer_subtype_information.BRCA1/2-mutated / HRD+: There is no known interaction between selpercatinib and BRCA status; no evidence links BRCA/HRD status to selpercatinib response.

notes: Breast-cancer–specific profiling data post-selpercatinib are described as scarce; several subtype statements are based on limited reports and extrapolation within the deep-research output. Contraindications: none listed in the deep-research output. Source files:
